text:
The Devils got the goalie everyone wanted. Connor Hellebuyck forced his way out of Winnipeg after a holdout, saying death threats motivated his trade request, and New Jersey is where he landed. When the Devils went back to Winnipeg this week they sat him, a decision that got its own news cycle.

The interesting part is that New Jersey hasn't needed him to steal anything. At 15-6-0 with 30 points, the Devils have a process to match the record: 58% of all expected goals (the quality of chances), 57% at five on five, and a penalty kill allowing only 0.47 expected goals a game while taking just 2.71 penalties. Results and chances agree almost exactly, which is the most reassuring thing a team can say in November.

Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Arseny Gritsyuk have outscored teams 12-5 with 62% of the chances. Nico Hischier's line with Timo Meier and Luke Evangelista controls play too. Luke Hughes, paired with Brett Pesce, is 19-9 in goals, the most dominant numbers on the blue line, and he traded punches with Matthew Schaefer in the Islanders game.

They swept a home-and-home with Washington, including a 7-4 win in which Evan Rodrigues scored twice, and trail Carolina for the Metropolitan lead. Our playoff odds sit at 96%. What we'd watch: how often Hellebuyck plays, and what he adds to a team already this good.
